Compare column types across data frames

Source: R/view_types.R
view_types.Rd

Shows the column types of one or more data frames side-by-side, and classifies each column by whether the datasets could be row-bound as they are. Useful for diagnosing type mismatches before a join or before binding with lazer::read_files().

Usage

view_types(..., diff = FALSE, focus = NULL)

Arguments

...

Data frames to compare (unquoted), or a single named list of data frames, such as the default output of lazer::read_files(). A list can also be spliced with !!!. Names are inferred from the expressions passed, or taken from the list.

diff

Logical. If TRUE, only columns with status "conflict" are shown, so frames that bind produce an empty result. To see every difference, filter on status != "ok" instead. Default: FALSE.

focus

A named character vector of expected types, e.g. c(cvr = "chr", year = "int"). When supplied, only the named columns are shown, and only for datasets where the type does not match (an absent column counts as a mismatch). Returns an empty tibble (0 rows) when all types match, so it can be used in checkpoints. Takes precedence over diff.

Value

A tibble with a column column, a status column (see Details) and one column per input dataset showing an abbreviated type string ("int", "dbl", "chr", "fct", "date", "dttm", ...). NA means the column is absent from that dataset.

Details

A type string alone does not say whether two data frames can be stacked: int and dbl bind without trouble, and so does a column that is entirely NA (readr reads an empty column as lgl). A column that is absent from one dataset is no obstacle either, since dplyr::bind_rows() fills it with NA. Only a real conflict such as chr vs dbl makes the bind fail, or forces lazer::read_files() to fall back to character. The status column therefore asks the question the function is called for: does it bind?

  • "ok": present everywhere with the same type.

  • "coercible": present everywhere, types differ but bind without loss of structure (int + dbl, fct + chr, date + dttm, an all-NA lgl with anything).

  • "missing": absent from at least one dataset, no conflict among the rest. Typically a rename or a dropped column upstream.

  • "conflict": the types cannot be combined.

Compatibility is tested by binding zero-row slices of each column with dplyr::bind_rows(), so the classification follows the same rules as read_files(out = "bind").

See also

lazer::read_files(), and expectr::expect_empty() to use view_types(diff = TRUE) or focus as a checkpoint

Examples

df1 <- data.frame(x = 1L,  y = "a", z = NA)
df2 <- data.frame(x = 1.0, y = 2,   z = "b")

view_types(df1, df2)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   column status    df1   df2  
#>   <chr>  <chr>     <chr> <chr>
#> 1 x      coercible int   dbl  
#> 2 y      conflict  chr   dbl  
#> 3 z      coercible lgl   chr  
view_types(df1, df2, diff = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   column status   df1   df2  
#>   <chr>  <chr>    <chr> <chr>
#> 1 y      conflict chr   dbl  
view_types(df1, df2, focus = c(x = "int", y = "chr"))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   column status    df2  
#>   <chr>  <chr>     <chr>
#> 1 x      coercible dbl  
#> 2 y      conflict  dbl  

# A named list of data frames, e.g. from read_files():
view_types(list(a = df1, b = df2))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   column status    a     b    
#>   <chr>  <chr>     <chr> <chr>
#> 1 x      coercible int   dbl  
#> 2 y      conflict  chr   dbl  
#> 3 z      coercible lgl   chr
